title: Playing with Peter Williams and Rabbit Brown
summary: Played professionally in small bands with Peter Williams, and briefly with Rabbit Brown, the clowning guitarist.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Did you play the guitar professionally?
Well, I made a living at it when I was playing.
Well, when I was playing, we had a little four piece band, five piece sometimes. I used to play with Peter Williams.
That's one of the old Dixieland musicians back on, he lived back on Gravy Street between White and Gauza. No, White and Dupree. White and Dupree. He lived on Gravy Street between White and Dupree.

That passed just two blocks, one block across James Allen. That's where Rabbit used to hang out. That's right. I know Rabbit. That's right. I played with Rabbit a couple of times, but Rabbit played so bad I had to let him go.

Yeah, he was mad, mad. Rabbit just hit the guitar and hollered. I mean his coat tail, he had a frock tail coat he used to wear, and that coat tail would be just sailing. He was what you call a clown man. He used to go out all out that, had mama loose, and things get tough out that, he didn't make no money. He'd call up the fire wagon, you know, and he knew all the guys was on the fire wagon. And he'd give them a false alarm, they'd all get out there and there wouldn't be no fire. And Rabbit would say, hey, how about riding back in town with y'all? That's how Rabbit is getting back. That's right. That's just the way he's getting back. I mean they got some old timers here to tell you all about it. But that's what them tell you. That's how rabbits get back in town.
